newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya security forces hunt killers of policemen.
newsitem.headline: Kenya security forces hunt killers of policemen.

text.p: Kenyan security forces hunted killers of seven policemen south of the Indian Ocean city of Mombasa on Friday and a security officer said the toll since Wednesday was at least 21 dead.
The officer, who declined to be identified, told Reuters the 21 people were killed in a raid on Wednesday night and attacks since then and seven police including three women were missing.
National Police Spokesman Peter Kimanthi said earlier six police and seven civilians including five attackers were killed in Wednesday's attack on police posts at Likoni just south of Mombasa.
Speaking in Nairobi, he said a seventh policeman had died on Thursday and one more civilian had died in the area on Friday.
"Those are the bodies we have in the mortuary. If there are other bodies in the bush we don't know about them," said Kimanthi, denying reports that any police had been abducted.
But the security officer told Reuters four dead civilians were found on Thursday night and two more were found in a pit near Likoni on Friday, taking the toll to at least 21 dead.
He said the policeman who died on Friday had a heart attack on operations and seven police including three women were missing. Nairobi newspapers said the policewomen were abducted.
Kimanthi said nine people were arrested on Friday in Kwale area near Matuga, taking the arrests since Wednesday to 43.

Men from Kenya's police, paramilitary General Service Unit (GSU), army and navy joined the manhunt backed by helicopters focusing on thick bush near Matuga village, 25 km (15 miles) south of Mombasa. Nearly all the village's residents had fled.
The area is hilly and also features some caves.

Mombasa police chief Francis Gichuki on Friday said four people were slashed to death by men armed with machetes in attacks on Thursday night and on Friday and one policeman was missing in action during clashes. He gave no Asked later about the numbers of dead and missing, he declined to comment and only said police were investigating.
Police and GSU stopped traffic on the main road from Mombasa to Tanzania for an hour after suspected gunmen were spotted.
The search operation involving hundreds of men stretched through a tourist haven from Mombasa to the Tanzanian border and was led by intelligence officers flown from the capital Nairobi.
Villagers said they saw youths armed with police issue G-3 rifles which were apparently stolen in Wednesday's raid when scores of attackers seized 28 G-3s and two sub-machineguns.
The Mombasa and Coast Tourist Association told hotels south of the port city on Friday to suspend their bus shuttles and tourists to stay on hotel property until security was restored.
The well-organised assailants on Wednesday burned down two police posts at Likoni in Mombasa and freed Kenyan prisoners.
Kenyan newspapers reflected confusion among officials and witnesses over the precise identity of the attackers who were described as "gangsters" on a night-long well-planned rampage.
But several slogans painted on walls near Matuga pointed to a political motive exacerabated by tribal and land tensions.
"These are not criminals. These are not thugs. Federalism," said one. "Federalism. Mainlanders should go to their homes," said another. "Federalism. Justice and Land," said a third.

Several hundred frightened local residents trekked on Friday to a Roman Catholic church compound at Likoni, carrying a few belongings on their heads. Many said they were too scared to talk to journalists because of the police and army presence.
Wednesday's attack was launched at a time of high political tension in Kenya ahead of a general election later this year.
